title: interop-fallback-matrix-and-compat-gap-action-plan
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers using the OpenAI Responses API expect specific streaming semantics, tool/function calling behavior, and structured output conventions that differ subtly from Redwood's native /responses runtime. Those differences cause interoperability problems in hosted and private deployments: broken tool calls, truncated JSON outputs, mismatched finish reasons that break client SDKs, and inconsistent event ordering for streaming consumers.

Scope: Produce a detailed compatibility matrix for the OpenAI Responses API surface versus Redwood's runtime (streaming frames, event types, function/tool calling payloads, structured output enforcement, content-type headers, stop sequences, finish_reason values, delta vs full message payloads). Implement a minimal runtime translation (interop layer) and a test harness for automated parity checks. Deliverables: 1) compatibility matrix CSV/Confluence page; 2) runtime fallback/translation design doc + small prototype adapter; 3) automated test suite with golden prompts and streaming capture; 4) rollout plan (canary + metrics + rollback).

Out of scope: Full replication of every historic OpenAI quirk (we will focus on behavior that currently breaks customers and major SDKs), changes to public SDKs beyond small shims, and protocol-level bundling for third-party proxies.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Mapping doc published and approved by PM and DX; 2) Prototype translation adapter can translate OpenAI-style function_call frames to Redwood tool invocation with >=95% fidelity on curated prompt corpus; 3) Streaming event order preserved and documented; 4) Test harness catches at least 3 previously-observed customer regressions; 5) Canary rollout produces no customer-facing errors during 72h at targeted traffic slice.
outcomes: Published compatibility matrix that enumerates concrete gaps and prioritized mitigations
Runtime adapter prototype that handles streaming SSE->chunk translation and function_call shim
Automated parity test harness integrated into CI with daily runs
Monitoring dashboards for rollback and error-class taxonomy
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Inventory and matrix creation; gather failing customer examples and SDK expectations. Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement prototype adapter that runs as a translation layer in front of Redwood runtime; focus on streaming frames, message role mapping, function_call arg extraction, and structured JSON completion enforcement. Phase 3 (1 week): End-to-end tests and canary. Phase 4 (monitoring + docs): Full rollout and postmortem. Owners: Liam O'Connor (runtime), Mei Zhang (tests), Priya Rao (DX docs).
test_plan: Create canonical prompt corpus from 12 customer incidents (streaming and tool calls)
Build harness to capture SSE fragments and reconstruct event timeline for assertions
Unit tests: mapping between OpenAI 'finish_reason' and Redwood finish flags (stop, length, error)
Integration tests: function_call roundtrip where OpenAI-style call is converted to Redwood tool invocation and tool result is fed back into stream as structured output
Regression tests: run nightly against latest runtime and flag new deltas with labels
monitoring: SLO: translated_requests error rate < 0.5% at canary traffic level
Dashboard: streaming event latency histogram and reordering rate
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Decided to implement translation as an opt-in adapter behind a feature flag rather than changing core runtime semantics (PM + Infra consensus)
2025-02-21: Prioritized streaming ordering and function_call arg fidelity as P0 mitigations; structured output strictness deferred to P1 unless it causes production breakage
2025-02-26: Agreed on canary policy: 1% traffic for 72h with automatic rollback if error rate exceeds threshold
